raw_extract:
# Residence Permit – Student

Your selection "third countries | student with notification of admission | no mobility programme | no agreement of higher education institutions | stay for more than 6 months" resulted in the following information:

# Residence Permit – Student

## Checklist

You have to enclose for the application photocopies of the following documents with your personally signed application form and additionally show only the originals:

- Valid Passport
- Passport-sized photograph according to the ICAO criteria (colour photograph, size 3.5 x 4.5 cm) not older than 6 months
- Proof of sufficient financial means to cover the living costs [as of 2026]:

  - Students under 24 years of age: EUR 722.58/month
  - Students as of the age of 24: EUR 1,308.39/month
  - Couples: EUR 2,064.12/month for both
  - For each child additionally: EUR 201,88/month

  You have to prove these funds for twelve months in advance. The funds have to be in a (foreign) savings book or (foreign) bank account that must bear the applicant's name and be accessible from Austria.
  An alternative possibility would be a declaration of guarantee ("Haftungserklaerung") of a person residing in the European Union, the purchase of traveller's cheques or a confirmation of the award of a scholarship.
  If the costs for accommodation exceed EUR 386,43/month [as of 2026], you have to prove additional funds. You also have to prove sufficient funds for the necessary health insurance.

- Declaration of regular expenses (loans, maintenance payments or other financial burdens)
- Accommodation in Austria for a minimum of 3 months (e.g. rental agreement, accommodation contract with a student hall of residence, accommodation agreement ["Wohnrechtsvereinbarung"]) in connexion with proof of the required funds to cover the living costs (the calculation is based on the presented costs for accomodation)
- Proof of health insurance covering all risks (e.g. by means of registration for student insurance after entry) in Austria

## Health insurance for entry and residence

For residence:

Degree programme students ("ordentliche Studierende") at all universities and universities of applied sciences ("Fachhochschulen") as well as non-degree programme students ("auesserordentliche Studierende") at University Preparation Programmes ("Vorstudienlehrgaenge") fulfil the requirement of a "health insurance covering all risks" if they take out student insurance ("Studierendenselbstversicherung") with the Oesterreichische Gesundheitskasse after entering Austria and enrolling at the higher education institution. The monthly insurance premium is EUR 78.84 [as of 2026].

## Period of validity

If all requirements are met, the "Residence Permit - Student" will be issued for a period of 12 months. If you applied for a shorter term or your travel document is valid for a shorter period of time, your residence permit will be issued for a shorter period.

## Working

An occupation that is subject to the Act Governing Employment of Foreign Nationals may only be carried out with a work permit ("Beschaeftigungsbewilligung").

Holders of a "Residence Permit - Student" will be able to get a work permit for working for up to 20 hours/week. This involves small-scale employment ("geringfuegige Beschaeftigung") as well. This permit will be granted without a labour market check.

## Renewal and change to another residence title

Students who have completed their studies holding a "Residence Permit - Student" may apply for a renewal of the permit for another 12 months to look for a job or set up a business.

## Costs

For applications one application fee of EUR 218 applies.
The complete fee must be paid when the application is submitted.

## Costs:

The decision period for the "Residence Permit-Student" is 90 days, but is extended by a further 90 days if additional documents need to be submitted!
research_notes:
Austria's financial-proof requirement for a student residence permit, as of 2026, AGE-BANDED. This is the single most decision-relevant Austrian finding in this pass: the required monthly amount depends on the applicant's AGE, not on the cost of a banded tuition. Two thresholds appear:

  - Students UNDER 24 years of age: EUR 722.58 per month
  - Students AS OF the age of 24: EUR 1,308.39 per month

That EUR 1,308.39 is materially higher than the 24-and-over figure a corpus might expect from a simple 'student' line item. It is because the Austrian student figure is derived from the general 'Ausgleichszulagenrichtsatz' (social assistance reference rate) for a single person, and the under-24 rate is a reduced student rate.

CORROBORATION FROM AN INDEPENDENT MINISTERIAL SOURCE, fetched separately: the Austrian Federal Ministry of the Interior page 'Voraussetzungen fuer die Erteilung von Aufenthaltstitel an Drittstaatsangehoerige' (https://www.bmi.gv.at/312/04/start.html, page footer 'Letzte Aktualisierung: 10. Februar 2026') gives the 2026 rates as 'Fuer Alleinstehende: EUR 1.308,39 / Fuer Ehepaare: EUR 2.064,12 / Fuer jedes Kind zusaetzlich: EUR 201,88' and explains that the amounts must be available net per month after deducting running costs such as rent or loan instalments. BMI does not restate the under-24 student rate on that page, so the OeAD checklist is the source for the age split.

RENT IS DEDUCTIBLE, and the deduction is capped. OeAD: 'If the costs for accommodation exceed EUR 386,43/month [as of 2026], you have to prove additional funds.' So the EUR 386.43 is the threshold of accommodation cost absorbable within the base rate; rent above that must be added to the required amount. Any Austrian first-year budget that ignores this will understate the required proof by the excess of actual rent over EUR 386.43.

FUNDS MUST COVER TWELVE MONTHS IN ADVANCE and sit in a savings book or account in the applicant's own name, accessible from Austria. Acceptable alternatives listed: a declaration of guarantee from an EU resident, traveller's cheques, or a scholarship confirmation. So a scholarship certificate IS accepted as the proof instrument, which is directly relevant to a scholarship corpus.

HEALTH INSURANCE, a first-year cost line: student self-insurance with the Austrian health insurance institution is EUR 78.84 per month as of 2026. Recorded here because it is verbatim on the same official checklist page and is compulsory.

APPLICATION COST: EUR 218, non-refundable. Recorded because the brief asks for auditable cost evidence and this one is on the official page.

WORK RIGHTS, on the same page: a student residence permit holder can get a work permit for up to 20 hours per week, including minor employment, granted without a labour market check. This is the Austrian figure and is distinct from Sweden's new 15-hour cap and Finland's 30-hour allowance; the three must not be merged.

PERMIT VALIDITY: 12 months for the standard (no mobility programme) student permit. Note that OeAD's separate mobility-programme page sets a different rule for two-year permits; I did not fetch that page and make no claim about it here beyond the validity of the standard permit.

conflict.note: NO CONFLICT. Two independent Austrian federal sources agree on the 24-and-over figure of EUR 1,308.39 per month and on the couple and per-child increments (EUR 2,064.12 and EUR 201.88). The two differ only in scope, not value: OeAD publishes the age-banded student checklist including the under-24 rate, while BMI publishes the general social-assistance reference rates for all residence titles without the student age split. Both are recorded because a corpus needs the student-specific figure and needs to know it sits on top of a general reference rate that applies to other permit types too.
